bibl.title: The Conceptual Definition of Sarcopenia: Delphi Consensus from the Global Leadership Initiative in Sarcopenia (GLIS)

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: A DEFINITION DECIDED BY VOTE, WITH EVERY VOTE PUBLISHED - 107 experts from 29 countries ranking statements about what sarcopenia IS, under a pre-specified agreement threshold, to harmonise six competing definitions into one
span.quote: The Global Leadership Initiative in Sarcopenia (GLIS) was formed in an attempt to harmonise these competing definitions into one unifying common classification that would be used as the gold standard in sarcopenia assessment.

span.label: which elements belong in the CONCEPT of sarcopenia, decided before and separately from how any of them would be measured
span.quote: The steering committee recognised that before any usable universal definition was derived, agreement on the concept of sarcopenia, including the elements that are key to defining the condition, was needed. Once these elements were agreed on, including these key framing concepts into a universal and usable definition would be facilitated [ 3 , 26 , 30 ]. It was agreed that this conceptual definition would use a modified Delphi process involving the GLIS group including several rounds until consensus was reached.

span.label: the first global CONCEPTUAL definition of sarcopenia - reduced muscle mass and muscle strength, plus muscle-specific strength, with physical performance placed outside the definition as an outcome and severity excluded entirely
span.quote: We agreed that the conceptual definition of sarcopenia comprises the concurrent combination of reduced muscle mass and muscle strength. We also found broad agreement that sarcopenia is a generalised disease of skeletal muscle; that prevalence of sarcopenia increases with age; that the definition of sarcopenia should not vary by setting of care, age or condition, or use (clinic vs. research); and that sarcopenia is a potentially reversible disease.

span.label: method
span.quote: Thresholds for agreement with statements were pre-specified by the steering committee as follows: low agreement (<70% respondents scoring ≥7), moderate agreement (70 to 80% respondents scoring ≥7) or strong agreement (>80% respondents scoring ≥7). Statements with strong agreement were accepted, and statements with low agreement were rejected. Statements with moderate agreement were reintroduced in the subsequent round until consensus was reached.

span.label: a construct whose membership is settled by percentage agreement among named experts, and whose boundary therefore sits at a threshold somebody chose
span.quote: Thresholds for agreement with statements were pre-specified by the steering committee as follows: low agreement (<70% respondents scoring ≥7), moderate agreement (70 to 80% respondents scoring ≥7) or strong agreement (>80% respondents scoring ≥7). Statements with strong agreement were accepted, and statements with low agreement were rejected. Statements with moderate agreement were reintroduced in the subsequent round until consensus was reached.

span.label: two-round modified Delphi: an 11-point Likert scale, agreement counted as the share scoring 7 or more, thresholds pre-specified at <70% / 70-80% / >80%, moderate statements reintroduced until consensus
span.term: two-round modified Delphi: an 11-point Likert scale, agreement counted as the share scoring 7 or more, thresholds pre-specified at <70% / 70-80% / >80%, moderate statements reintroduced until consensus
span.quote: Thresholds for agreement with statements were pre-specified by the steering committee as follows: low agreement (<70% respondents scoring ≥7), moderate agreement (70 to 80% respondents scoring ≥7) or strong agreement (>80% respondents scoring ≥7). Statements with strong agreement were accepted, and statements with low agreement were rejected. Statements with moderate agreement were reintroduced in the subsequent round until consensus was reached.

span.label: **THE ELEMENT THAT MOVED FROM BEING PART OF THE THING TO BEING CAUSED BY IT**: `impaired physical performance was accepted as an `OUTCOME` (Sarcopenia INCREASES THE RISK OF impaired physical performance (97.9%)) RATHER THAN A `COMPONENT` of sarcopenia (Physical performance should be part of the conceptual definition of sarcopenia (79.4%))`. In EWGSOP 2010 - paper 64 in this corpus - LOW PHYSICAL PERFORMANCE IS CRITERION 3, a diagnostic component. Fourteen years later the same element is a consequence. **One relation, two of this corpus's edge types, and the vote that moved it is printed to one decimal place**
span.quote: Furthermore, impaired physical performance was accepted as an ‘outcome’ (Sarcopenia increases the risk of impaired physical performance (97.9%)) rather than a ‘component’ of sarcopenia (Physical performance should be part of the conceptual definition of sarcopenia (79.4%)). Altogether, this suggests that a conceptual definition of sarcopenia would include muscle mass, strength and muscle-specific strength as components.

span.label: AND THE THRESHOLD IS PRE-SPECIFIED, SO THE BOUNDARY OF THE CONCEPT IS A NUMBER SOMEBODY CHOSE: `low agreement (<70% respondents scoring >=7), moderate agreement (70 to 80%) or strong agreement (>80%). STATEMENTS WITH STRONG AGREEMENT WERE ACCEPTED, and statements with low agreement were REJECTED. Statements with moderate agreement were REINTRODUCED in the subsequent round until consensus was reached.` Muscle-specific strength entered at 80.8%; physical performance was excluded at 79.8%. **ONE PERCENTAGE POINT OF A 107-PERSON SURVEY DECIDES WHAT THE DISEASE IS**
span.quote: Thresholds for agreement with statements were pre-specified by the steering committee as follows: low agreement (<70% respondents scoring ≥7), moderate agreement (70 to 80% respondents scoring ≥7) or strong agreement (>80% respondents scoring ≥7). Statements with strong agreement were accepted, and statements with low agreement were rejected. Statements with moderate agreement were reintroduced in the subsequent round until consensus was reached.

span.label: AND THE PAPER SAYS THE MARGIN OUT LOUD: `The overall support for inclusion of specific strength ... was ONLY SLIGHTLY HIGHER THAN OUR THRESHOLD FOR AGREEMENT - 80.8% SUPPORTED ITS INCLUSION WHEN THE THRESHOLD IS 80%, AND THIS STATEMENT DID NOT MEET THE THRESHOLD IN THE FIRST ROUND.` A component of the definition admitted by eight tenths of a point, on a second attempt, and the authors flag it as something the operational phase may undo
span.quote: The overall support for inclusion of specific strength in the conceptual definition for sarcopenia was only slightly higher than our threshold for agreement—80.8% supported its inclusion when the threshold is 80%, and this statement did not meet the threshold in the first round. Therefore, in the next steps of GLIS, we will carefully consider whether an operational definition includes all three measures (muscle mass, strength and specific strength) or just two measures (muscle mass and strength) or just one (muscle-specific strength).

span.label: AND ONE STATEMENT WAS REJECTED BECAUSE A DIFFERENT ONE FAILED: `Statement 5 `The conceptual definition of sarcopenia should include LEVELS OF SEVERITY` was rejected with an agreement of 77.0% ... AS STATEMENT 5 DID NOT MEET THE ACCEPTANCE THRESHOLD (>80%), THE REMAINING FOUR STATEMENTS RELATING TO `MARKERS OF THE SEVERITY OF SARCOPENIA` WERE REJECTED.` The vote that removed them is not a vote about them
span.quote: Statement 5 ‘The conceptual definition of sarcopenia should include levels of severity of the disease’ was rejected with an agreement of 77.0% (mean score: 7.1 ± 2.7, n = 107 respondents). As statement 5 did not meet the acceptance threshold (>80%), the remaining four (50%) statements relating to ‘markers of the severity of sarcopenia’ were rejected. Note that these four statements were optional as specified in the survey guidelines.

span.label: AND ONE OF THE FOUR HAD PASSED: `Physical performance should be A MARKER OF SEVERITY for the conceptual definition of sarcopenia. AGREEMENT: 81.9% (mean score: 7.6 +/- 2.4; answered = 93, skipped = 14).` **Above the 80% threshold, and rejected anyway**, because the statement it depended on scored 77.0%. A dependency between statements that the threshold rule does not model
span.quote: 4. ‘ Physical performance should be a marker of severity for the conceptual definition of sarcopenia’. Agreement: 81.9% (mean score: 7.6 ± 2.4; answered = 93, skipped = 14) ( Figure 2 ).

span.label: AND THE INSTRUMENT WAS DELIBERATELY REMOVED FROM THE QUESTION: `TO AVOID THE ISSUE THAT ANSWERS MIGHT BE SKEWED BY THE ACCURACY AND LACK OF CURRENTLY AVAILABLE MEASUREMENT METHODS, EXPERTS WERE ASKED TO ASSUME THAT PERFECT, FEASIBLE ASSESSMENTS OF EACH LISTED MEASURE EXISTED.` A consensus body explicitly preventing the apparatus from shaping the concept - the inverse of leslie2022, where a construct is bounded by a filter pore. And they knew it had been happening
span.quote: To avoid the issue that answers might be skewed by the accuracy and lack of currently available measurement methods, experts were asked to assume that perfect, feasible assessments of each listed measure existed.

span.label: BECAUSE THE EARLIER DISAGREEMENTS WERE PARTLY ABOUT INSTRUMENTS AND PARTLY ABOUT WORDS: `some of the differences in previous definitions were related to disagreements on WHETHER MUSCLE MASS SHOULD BE INCLUDED IN THE DEFINITION PARTLY DUE TO MEASUREMENT ISSUES OF AVAILABLE TECHNIQUES ..., WHETHER PHYSICAL FUNCTION SHOULD BE CONSIDERED AS PART OF THE DEFINITION OR AS AN OUTCOME, and around the concept of muscle quality. In addition, SOME TERMS WERE NOT WELL DEFINED IN THE LITERATURE ... the term `SARCOPENIA` HAD BEEN USED TO REFER TO LOW MUSCLE MASS ALONE in some studies. FOR THIS REASON, THE FIRST PRODUCT OF THE GLIS INITIATIVE WAS A GLOSSARY OF TERMS.` A working group whose first output is a vocabulary, because the vocabulary was the obstacle
span.quote: In the first meetings, the steering committee explored the issues that had to be addressed in the search for a global consensus. It became evident that some of the differences in previous definitions were related to disagreements on whether muscle mass should be included in the definition partly due to measurement issues of available techniques and their association with outcomes, whether physical function should be considered as part of the definition or as an outcome, and around the concept of muscle quality [ 26 , 27 ]. In addition, some terms were not well defined in the literature. As an example, many different definitions of muscle quality were used in previous studies, and the term ‘sarcopenia’ had been used to refer to low muscle mass alone in some studies and to the loss of muscle mass with ageing without consideration of function [ 28 ]. For this reason, the first product of the GLIS initiative was a glossary of terms used in sarcopenia research and practice [ 29 ].

span.label: AND THE 2010 ADMINISTRATIVE GAP IS HALF CLOSED, IN THE OTHER ORDER: `Sarcopenia ALSO LACKS A GLOBAL AND WIDELY ACCEPTED DEFINITION that can be routinely used in clinical settings, EVEN THOUGH AN ICD10-CM CODE FOR THIS CONDITION EXISTS.` cruz-jentoft2010 listed the missing ICD-9 code beside the missing definition. **THE CODE ARRIVED FIRST** - in one national modification, not in the classification itself
span.quote: Sarcopenia also lacks a global and widely accepted definition that can be routinely used in clinical settings, even though an ICD10-CM code for this condition exists [ 5 ].

span.label: AND THE STANDARDS BODY TOLD THEM WHAT WOULD CLOSE THE REST: `The WHO was also contacted, and WE WERE INFORMED THAT A GLOBAL DEFINITION WOULD FACILITATE INCLUSION OF SARCOPENIA IN THE INTERNATIONAL CLASSIFICATION OF DISEASES (at present it is only included in the Clinical Modification version of ICD).` The definition is being written partly IN ORDER TO obtain a code - the vocabulary and its administrative slot pulling on each other, stated by both parties
span.quote: The WHO was also contacted, and we were informed that a global definition would facilitate inclusion of sarcopenia in the International Classification of Diseases (at present it is only included in the Clinical Modification version of ICD) [ 25 ].

span.label: THE REASON TO AGREE ON A WORD IS ADMINISTRATIVE RECOGNITION: `the World Health Organization (WHO) HAS YET TO INCLUDE AN ICD-10 CODE for sarcopenia ... A GLOBAL DEFINITION of sarcopenia WOULD EASE THE ADOPTION OF AN ICD-10 CODE by WHO, which, IN TURN, WOULD INCREASE CLINICAL RECOGNITION of this condition worldwide.` The chain runs definition -> code -> recognition, and the paper states it in that order.
span.quote: Although the ICD10-CM code is available in some countries such as Australia and the United States, the World Health Organization (WHO) has yet to include an ICD-10 code for sarcopenia in its version. A global definition of sarcopenia would ease the adoption of an ICD-10 code for sarcopenia by WHO, which, in turn, would increase clinical recognition of this condition worldwide

span.label: AND CONCEPTUAL AGREEMENT IS SEQUENCED BEFORE OPERATIONAL AGREEMENT, DELIBERATELY: `The NEXT STEP in the coming years of GLIS is to develop AN OPERATIONAL DEFINITION for clinical and research settings FROM THE AGREED-UPON CONCEPTUAL DEFINITION formed by the Delphi process.` Every other chain in this corpus revises criteria and thresholds together; this one splits meaning from measurement and does meaning first.
span.quote: The next step in the coming years of GLIS is to develop an operational definition for clinical and research settings from the agreed-upon conceptual definition formed by the Delphi process

span.label: SIX DEFINITIONS AND THE REPAIR IS A SEVENTH BODY: `Several groups have proposed definitions of sarcopenia, including the AWGS, the ANZSSFR, the EWGSOP that issued guidelines in 2010 that were REVISED IN 2019; the FNIH Sarcopenia Project, the IWGS and the SDOC`. The response to six competing committees is to convene a global one - the same move ISAPP made for `prebiotic` after five definitions.
span.quote: Several groups have proposed definitions of sarcopenia, including the Asian Working Group for Sarcopenia (AWGS) [ 12 , 13 ], the Australian and New Zealand Society for Sarcopenia and Frailty Research (ANZSSFR) [ 14 , 15 ], the European Working Group for Sarcopenia in Older Persons (EWGSOP) that issued guidelines in 2010 [ 16 ] that were revised in 2019 [ 17 ]; the Foundation for the National Institutes of Health (FNIH) Sarcopenia Project [ 18 ], the International Working Group on Sarcopenia (IWGS) [ 19 ] and the Sarcopenia Definitions and Outcomes Consortium (SDOC) that issued operational cut-off points in several measures that characterise sarcopenia in 2020

span.label: THE ACCEPTED COMPONENTS OVERLAP AND THE PAPER SAYS SO: `A CHALLENGE THAT WAS NOT PREVIOUSLY CONSIDERED when developing the Delphi statements is how to consider these POTENTIALLY OVERLAPPING COMPONENTS, WHERE MUSCLE MASS AND STRENGTH MAY BE THE SAME COMPONENTS INCLUDED IN THE SPECIFIC STRENGTH MEASURE.` Muscle-specific strength is strength standardised to size, so voting all three in may have voted the same two in twice - a defect in the definition discovered after the vote that produced it
span.quote: A challenge that was not previously considered when developing the Delphi statements is how to consider these potentially overlapping components, where muscle mass and strength may be the same components included in the specific strength measure.

span.label: AND THE PROXY THE OPERATIONAL DEFINITION WILL HAVE TO USE IS DISPUTED: `the SDOC found that there is SUBSTANTIAL DISAGREEMENT REGARDING THE USE OF LEAN MASS MEASURED BY DXA AS A PROXY OF MUSCLE MASS: on one hand, LEAN MASS IS WIDELY MEASURED AND CLINICALLY AVAILABLE; while on the other hand, IT DOES NOT DIRECTLY MEASURE MUSCLE MASS, and its associations with sarcopenia-related outcomes (mortality, fractures, falls, disability) ARE WEAK OR INCONSISTENT.` The concept was defined with the instrument assumed perfect; the instrument is neither perfect nor agreed
span.quote: For example, in previous work, the SDOC found that there is substantial disagreement regarding the use of lean mass measured by DXA as a proxy of muscle mass: on one hand, lean mass is widely measured and clinically available; while on the other hand, it does not directly measure muscle mass, and its associations with sarcopenia-related outcomes (mortality, fractures, falls, disability) are weak or inconsistent [ 1 , 20 , 21 ].

span.label: and the conceptual definition is explicitly NOT usable yet: `The next phase of GLIS will include the OPERATIONALIZATION of the newly developed conceptual definition` - so the paper defines the condition and defers every cut-off point, which is the exact reverse of cruz-jentoft2010, whose Table 5 is nothing but cut-off points
span.quote: The steering committee recognised that before any usable universal definition was derived, agreement on the concept of sarcopenia, including the elements that are key to defining the condition, was needed. Once these elements were agreed on, including these key framing concepts into a universal and usable definition would be facilitated [ 3 , 26 , 30 ]. It was agreed that this conceptual definition would use a modified Delphi process involving the GLIS group including several rounds until consensus was reached.

span.label: and a 52% response rate with a European majority: `The GLIS included reasonable representation of men and women, and geography, ALTHOUGH MOST OF THE RESPONDENTS WERE FROM EUROPE. The total response rate of GLIS was 52% ... WHICH COULD HAVE BEEN HIGHER. Nevertheless, we retained 100% (107/107) of participants through both rounds`. Both conceded in the strengths paragraph
span.quote: The GLIS included reasonable representation of men and women, and geography, although most of the respondents were from Europe. The total response rate of GLIS was 52% (107/206 participants originally invited agreed to participate) which could have been higher. Nevertheless, we retained 100% (107/107) of participants through both rounds of the Delphi process which is another strength of our study.

span.label: instructing the experts to ASSUME PERFECT, FEASIBLE ASSESSMENTS of each listed measure existed
span.note: eliminates: answers skewed by which measurements happen to be accurate or available - the apparatus deciding the concept · outcome: held
span.quote: To avoid the issue that answers might be skewed by the accuracy and lack of currently available measurement methods, experts were asked to assume that perfect, feasible assessments of each listed measure existed.

span.label: pre-specifying the agreement thresholds (<70% / 70-80% / >80%) before the survey ran
span.note: eliminates: a threshold chosen after the votes were seen · outcome: held
span.quote: Thresholds for agreement with statements were pre-specified by the steering committee as follows: low agreement (<70% respondents scoring ≥7), moderate agreement (70 to 80% respondents scoring ≥7) or strong agreement (>80% respondents scoring ≥7). Statements with strong agreement were accepted, and statements with low agreement were rejected. Statements with moderate agreement were reintroduced in the subsequent round until consensus was reached.

span.label: a glossary of sarcopenia terms published BEFORE the Delphi statements were voted on
span.note: eliminates: experts agreeing on a statement while meaning different things by its words - `many different definitions of muscle quality were used in previous studies` · outcome: partial
span.quote: In the first meetings, the steering committee explored the issues that had to be addressed in the search for a global consensus. It became evident that some of the differences in previous definitions were related to disagreements on whether muscle mass should be included in the definition partly due to measurement issues of available techniques and their association with outcomes, whether physical function should be considered as part of the definition or as an outcome, and around the concept of muscle quality [ 26 , 27 ]. In addition, some terms were not well defined in the literature. As an example, many different definitions of muscle quality were used in previous studies, and the term ‘sarcopenia’ had been used to refer to low muscle mass alone in some studies and to the loss of muscle mass with ageing without consideration of function [ 28 ]. For this reason, the first product of the GLIS initiative was a glossary of terms used in sarcopenia research and practice [ 29 ].

We also found broad agreement that sarcopenia is a generalised disease of skeletal muscle; that prevalence of sarcopenia increases with age; that the definition of sarcopenia should not vary by setting of care, age or condition, or use (clinic vs. research); and that sarcopenia is a potentially reversible disease.

In lotvall2014 the gold standard is DENIED to exist; in doyle2019 it is AWARDED to an incumbent; here it is a DELIVERABLE.

span.quote: A key finding of the Delphi survey was that muscle mass, muscle strength and muscle-specific strength were all accepted as ‘components of sarcopenia’, whereas impaired physical performance was accepted as an ‘outcome’ rather than a ‘component’ of sarcopenia. Conclusion and relevance The GLIS has created the first global conceptual definition of sarcopenia, which will now serve to develop an operational definition for clinical and research settings. span.label: extends → the six competing regional definitions of sarcopenia - AWGS, ANZSSFR, EWGSOP (2010, revised 2019), FNIH, IWGS and SDOC - which GLIS was formed to harmonise into one classification
span.quote: The Global Leadership Initiative in Sarcopenia (GLIS) was formed in an attempt to harmonise these competing definitions into one unifying common classification that would be used as the gold standard in sarcopenia assessment.

span.quote: We agreed that the conceptual definition of sarcopenia comprises the concurrent combination of reduced muscle mass and muscle strength. We also found broad agreement that sarcopenia is a generalised disease of skeletal muscle; that prevalence of sarcopenia increases with age; that the definition of sarcopenia should not vary by setting of care, age or condition, or use (clinic vs. research); and that sarcopenia is a potentially reversible disease.
